ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L.561-1 et seq., L.561-4, L.561-10, L.561-46 et seq.), Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020, Sapin II law n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016, Décret n° 2018-284 du 18 avril 2018, Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; obligation to identify and report UBOs under R.561-17 and R.561-21.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each direct shareholder, manager (gérant), and each ultimate beneficial owner holding at least 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent state authority in the country of origin (police, prefecture, or national identity authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a Hague Convention member; otherwise consular legalization at the French embassy or consulate with official French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and registry extract of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization by the receiving French authority; followed by certified translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the French incorporation agent or attorney, executed by each shareholder and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or public authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization in non-apostille jurisdictions, with French certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal conviction / police clearance record for any individual manager or appointed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or police authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; French sworn translation mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the corporate constitutional documents (statuts, by-laws, shareholders' register) of any non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official registry or public notary in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified translation into French required for registration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all direct shareholders, managers, and UBOs against the EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, French national asset-freeze registers (DG Trésor/FI-FI), and TRACFIN advisories; PEP status assessed in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and EU Directive (EU) 2015/849; automated sanctions-screening software with documented alert disposition and escalation to the AML compliance officer; enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth/statatory-funds verification required for any PEP, sanction hit, or adverse media finding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique / INPI Formalitès Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with name conflict verification performed against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and INPI Data databases
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in French or in a language expressible in Latin script; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a French translation in the deed; all foreign-language corporate documents must be translated by a certified legal translator unless an official French version is provided; the name must be legal, not contrary to public order, and must not mislead the public as to the legal form or activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of a rejection notice or the effective refusal of registration by the greffier, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the same registry based on newly furnished evidence or correction of the name. If the name remains refused, an interim application (référé) may be filed before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce to stay or rectify the registry decision; a substantive appeal to the Tribunal de Commerce and, subsequently, to the Cour d'appel is available under Articles R.123-128, R.123-131 and R.123-147 of the Code de commerce. The applicant must simultaneously notify any prior trademark owner or distinct identity claimant and may seek court-ordered change of the registered name in contentious proceedings without a penalty if acted expeditiously.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk EdTech subscription business provided that the registered office is a commercial domiciliation company duly authorized by the Préfecture or a business centre meeting the requirements of Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-165 of the Code de commerce; the address must be a real physical place capable of receiving official mail and allowing access for authorities; a contractual company-seat lease and a written acknowledgment of domiciliation must be maintained; pure mailbox services without a physical reception capacity are not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk of unannounced physical inspection by social, tax, or registry authorities is approximately 10% per annum for a standard EdTech service entity with no high-risk AML factors; the likelihood increases to approximately 25% where the entity relies solely on a virtual office, has no local employees or assets, and evidence of commercial substance cannot be produced on request.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compulsory legal announcement of incorporation in a French official legal gazette (JAL / journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal-announcement publisher registered with the CPPAP
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory advertisement tariff set by the publisher, typically EUR 90-140 per notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration filing fee at the Guichet Unique / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), including the droit de greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated court registry fee scale for commercial entity formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fees for review of corporate resolutions, certification of capacity, and notarization of French-language corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee schedule for auxiliary corporate acts, supplemented by time-based charges at EUR 150-400 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration preparation and filing (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) integrated with the company formation dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff for the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille / consular legalization and certified translation of foreign corporate existence documents, passports, and clearances
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Consular authority or designated competent authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction; French certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular legalization fee schedule plus certified translator fee of EUR 80-120 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and trademark preliminary search against INPI Data, RNE, and domain registries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial court registry / IP trademark attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for automated multi-jurisdiction clearance search, EUR 50-180

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual office / domiciliation service for a 12-month subscription at an authorized business centre in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company approved by the Préfecture or registered business centre
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for approved domiciliation in Paris or major French city, EUR 60-150 per month

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External AML/CFT compliance counsel fee for pre-incorporation UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, source-of-funds review, and preparation of the due diligence file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML/CFT compliance counsel / licensed attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed package or hourly rate of EUR 200-350 per hour for attorney work

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Code de commerce, Book II: Articles L.210-2 (subscription and payment of share capital), L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation and governance), R.223-1 to R.223-29; Décret n°84-406 on the registre du commerce et des sociétés; Articles L.123-3 and R.123-1 et seq. on company registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce territorially competent for the registered office, acting through the Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise using Cerfa n°14777 (M0), submitted electronically as a single formalities dossier through the Guichet unique INPI and transmitted to the commercial registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital is freely fixed (statutory floor of EUR 1). All shares must be subscribed at formation; cash contributions must be paid up to at least 20% at incorporation and the balance may be paid within five years; in-kind contributions must be fully released upon formation. Where funds are deposited before registration, the manager must open an escrow or blocked capital account and obtain a bank or notarial attestation de dépôt des fonds, which is attached to the incorporation file and released only after issuance of the Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST DECISION OF THE ASSOCIATES, ADOPTED [DATE]. 1. The statutes are approved. The shares shown in the capital table are subscribed and allocated; cash contributions are paid up to the minimum required by law and, where applicable, the blocked deposit attestation is approved. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], within the jurisdiction of the Greffe du tribunal de commerce de [city]. 3. [Name] is appointed gérant with all powers to manage, represent and bind the company, under Article L.223-18 of the Commercial Code. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private deed signed by all associates; optional public deed before a notary if the contribution includes real property.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles under L.223-1 et seq., including legal form, corporate object, duration (maximum 99 years), share capital, cash and in-kind contributions, registered office, management powers and share allocation. All associates or their authorised attorneys must sign the final executed copy. If an in-kind contribution is made, the statutory contributions appraiser's report must be annexed in accordance with Article L.223-9.
required_dossiers: Draft final articles of association
Identity documents for all associates and the proposed manager
Valuation report of the in-kind contribution appraiser, if applicable
Power of attorney if a representative signs
Domiciliation certificate for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a third party identifies a defect, execute a rectificatory deed amending the articles and refile the corrected version; no refund is available after the initial filing is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked share-capital deposit account and obtaining the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, mutual bank, or notary acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation, deposit at least the statutory 20% of cash contributions (or the full amount if so provided in the articles), and obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds. The funds remain blocked until the Kbis is issued and may then be released to the gérant on presentation of the registration extract.
required_dossiers: Draft or signed extract of the articles of association
Identity documents of associates and managers
KYC questionnaire and beneficial ownership information
Bank coordinates and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, provide the capital structure table, the draft articles and the beneficial owner declaration; the bank may reissue the deposit attestation once the final signed deed is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation announcement in an approved legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorised by the prefecture of the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place an avis de constitution containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate object, duration, manager identity and place of registration with the commercial registry. Obtain the proof of publication or publication receipt from the legal-journal publisher and include it in the formation dossier.
required_dossiers: Final text of the legal announcement
Draft articles of association or a copy of the executed statutes
Identity details of the manager
Registered office address and registry assignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is refused or defective, correct the wording and publish a new or corrective notice in another authorised legal gazette; submit the corrective publication proof to the registry if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the incorporation dossier to the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises administered by INPI, with substantive control by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet unique, select company creation, complete the Cerfa M0 declaration, upload all required attachments, pay the electronic greffe fee, and submit. The Guichet transmits the dossier to the territorial commercial registry and, after registration, to INSEE for SIREN/SIRET assignment and to URSSAF for social notifications.
required_dossiers: Cerfa M0 declaration
Signed final articles of association
Bank or notarial deposit attestation for cash contributions
Proof of legal announcement publication
Registered office occupation or domiciliation certificate
Identity documents of managers and beneficial owners, or the R.123-14 beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an irregularity notice, the applicant must file corrections through the Guichet unique within the prescribed cure period and resubmit the corrected documents; failure to cure results in deemed abandonment and a new application must be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Kbis extract, SIREN/SIRET registration and administrative notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce and Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques (INSEE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation, the commercial registry registers the company in the registre du commerce et des sociétés and issues the extrait Kbis. INSEE assigns the SIREN and SIRET identifiers. The company must retain the Kbis in its corporate register and use the SIRET number for invoicing, payroll and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Registration confirmation from the Guichet unique
INSEE SIREN/SIRET assignment notice
Original Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed beyond the applicable SLA, the company may petition the président du tribunal de commerce to fix a completion deadline; any SIRENE data discrepancy must be corrected through a modification form on the Guichet unique.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no physical manufacturing or industrial establishment is created; the prefecture and DREAL would intervene only if the company later opens classified premises under the ICPE regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating or manufacturing license is required for EdTech software publishing and automated language tutoring under ISIC 6201; the only mandatory formalities are RCS registration, GDPR compliance, and, where applicable, consumer and e-commerce disclosure obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) and the Préfecture de département — applicable only if future physical infrastructure becomes an installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is required for pure software publication; the activity does not fall under the ICPE nomenclature and no qualifying industrial process is operated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge, VOC or wastewater thresholds apply. The company must nonetheless manage office waste through municipal collection and route electrical and electronic equipment waste exclusively to registered DEEE collectors, while maintaining electrical safety compliance in leased premises in accordance with NF C 15-100 and Code du travail requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office and administrative workplace, the company must hold the landlord's premises occupancy clearance, verify structural and fire-safety conformity, provide fire extinguishers and evacuation procedures under Code du travail Articles R.4227-1 et seq., ensure work access safety under Article R.4224-1, and maintain an electrical installation conformity check under Article R.4216-1. No additional civil-defence clearance is required for a software-as-a-service operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy and Finance, France; tax portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); customs and export VAT controls: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL: (1) incorporate via the Guichet Unique portal, which automatically issues the SIREN and SIRET identifiers and the intra-community VAT number (FR+11 digits); (2) file the DPAE for the legal representative and complete non-resident director documentation; (3) open a French bank account and notify the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for corporate income tax (IS) registration; (4) for foreign non-established entities supplying digital services to French consumers, register for French VAT via the DGFiP foreign-entities desk (Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères) using the online non-resident registration module, or elect the EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) to obtain an OSS VAT identifier; (5) where physical goods are exported, obtain an EORI number (DGDDI) and, if required, a customs broker mandate; lead time is typically 2 to 6 weeks for standard VAT/IS registration, while OSS registration is granted within a few days upon online application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (IS) at 25%, with a reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover below EUR 10,000,000. Statutory elections available: (a) option for pass-through taxation under Article 239 bis A of the French General Tax Code (CGI) for close-held small SARLs with fewer than 50 employees and turnover or total assets not exceeding EUR 10,000,000, effective for a maximum of 5 consecutive fiscal years; (b) French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for a group of companies where the parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary's share capital; (c) election to be subject to VAT even when below the small-business franchise threshold; (d) no US-style check-the-box mechanism exists; hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatches are instead neutralized through domestic anti-hybrid provisions (Articles 205 bis and 212 bis CGI) implementing EU Directive 2016/1164, which deny deductions and impose symmetrical classification for entities treated as transparent in one jurisdiction but opaque in France.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic franchise en base de TVA: EUR 91,900 for goods and EUR 36,800 for services per year; EdTech subscription services (digitally supplied) are treated as services, so the EUR 36,800 threshold applies to a French-established micro-business; however, EU cross-border B2C digital services supplied by an EU-established supplier trigger mandatory OSS registration once the EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-sales/digital-services threshold is exceeded; non-EU established suppliers have a zero threshold and must register for French VAT or the EU OSS/IOSS from the first euro of French taxable turnover; an active French SARL engaged in EdTech B2C subscriptions must register for VAT immediately unless it validly relies on the franchise, and must in any event register if it intends to charge VAT, issue VAT invoices, or recover input VAT under the normal regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Loi de Finances 2020; specification published by the arrêté of 29 July 2024): from 1 September 2026, large and mid-size entities must issue B2B e-invoices and all French VAT-registered businesses must receive them electronically; from 1 September 2027, all VAT payers, including foreign companies registered for French VAT, must issue e-invoices; supported formats are Factur-X, UBL, and CII; exchange routes are through a certified Dematerialization Partner Platform (PDP) or the free Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); invoices must be transmitted to the DGFiP via the PDP/PPF within one business day of issuance; e-reporting data for B2C, intra-EU, and export transactions is filed monthly by the 10th day of the following month; there is no real-time digital stamping or serialization of each invoice as in Latin American fiscal clearance models; instead, France applies transactional batch control through the PPF/PDP ecosystem, supplemented by the mandatory FEC (Fichier des Écritures Comptables) accounting-file obligation and certified anti-tamper cash-register software for POS retail; marketplace sellers must also consider the deemed-supplier rules under Article 242 bis CGI where the platform is treated as the taxable seller.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical goods: 0% French VAT applies where the exporter lodges a customs export declaration (DAU), the goods physically leave EU territory within 90 days of supply, and transport documentation is maintained (Article 262-I CGI; EU VAT Directive Articles 146-147). EdTech subscriptions (electronically supplied services): the goods-style zero-rating mechanism is not used; supplies to non-EU B2C customers are outside the scope of French VAT because the place of supply is the customer's country of residence (Article 259 D CGI); supplies to EU or non-EU B2B customers are shifted to the customer's VAT account under reverse charge (Article 259-1 CGI; Article 44 EU VAT Directive); for EU B2C cross-border digital services, the French supplier applies the consumer's Member State VAT rate through the OSS return and cannot claim zero rating; the supplier must substantiate customer location via IP address, bank details, billing address, SIM card country code, landline location, or other commercially reasonable evidence as set out in the EU VAT administrative cooperation guidance; for app-store sales (Apple IAP / Google Play), the platform operator may self-assume the VAT liability as deemed supplier, and the French publisher must reconcile the associated net settlements against the VAT treatment applicable to each app-store territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU / Document Administratif Unique) lodged electronically in the DELTA system and accepted by DGDDI
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice incorporating the exact Incoterms, export VAT exempt annotation ('Exportation - Hors champ TVA, Article 262-I CGI') and the customer's industrial/commercial status
Proof of settlement and inward remittance certificate (bank SWIFT/IBAN statement or Bank Payment Obligation) evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Supply-chain substantiation file: purchase and delivery records, customs valuation dossier, packing lists, and internal transport instructions retained for audit defense
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT zero-rating claims are subject to intensive scrutiny by DGFiP and DGDDI. Failure to produce the mandatory documentation bundle within 30 days of an audit request exposes the exporter to immediate VAT regularisation, output VAT on the full invoice amount, intérêts de retard at 0.20% per month, and penalties of 40% for lack of good faith, 80% for deliberate tax fraud (mauvaise foi / manœuvres frauduleuses), and up to 100% for organized fraud chains (Article 1729 CGI). Customs violations for fictional or false export declarations carry confiscation of the goods and transport means, fines of one to two times the value of the object of fraud (Code des douanes Articles 413-1 to 414-2), and criminal imprisonment, which can reach 10 years for organized smuggling; on the tax side, Article 1741 CGI criminal tax fraud is punishable by a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment, increased to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years when committed by an organized group. Claims are clawed back retroactively across the applicable limitation windows (generally 3 years under Article L.176 CGI-LPF for VAT, extended to 6 years where the activity is conducted abroad under Articles L.169-LPF for direct taxes); therefore all export zero-rating evidence, FX repatriation records, and app-store settlement statements must be retained for a minimum of 10 years, with particular attention to the 180-day FX repatriation deadline as a compliance red flag when exceeded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking supervision; FX policy is set by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, with operational oversight by the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the Eurozone and the EU, with the euro (EUR) as legal tender. The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. France adheres to OECD and EU liberalization codes, and there are no general restrictions on capital movements. However, certain transactions require reporting to the Banque de France for statistical and balance-of-payments purposes, particularly for direct investment, real estate, and loans exceeding €15,000. Profit remittances (dividends, royalties, interest) are freely transferable subject to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable) and anti-money laundering (AML) verification. No prior exchange control approval is required for current account payments, but documentation must be retained to evidence the underlying transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency earnings in bank accounts, either in France or abroad, subject to reporting obligations. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation, but all cross-border transactions must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics if they exceed €50,000 per transaction or €150,000 per calendar year in aggregate. The euro is the functional currency; conversion of foreign currency receipts is at the discretion of the company, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) and potentially a Capital Escrow Account for initial share capital deposit
Operational Account and dedicated FX settlement account
Operational Account and trade finance facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) under the EU PSD2 framework, regulated by the ACPR. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., those licensed in Lithuania, UK, or Singapore) can operate in France under passporting rights if they are EU-licensed, but they are not full banks and may not offer credit or deposit facilities. For an EdTech company with subscription revenue, an EMI can handle payment processing and FX conversion, but for treasury management and capital injection, a full bank account is recommended. Legal constraints: EMIs must comply with French AML/CFT regulations and may require a local agent for KYC. They cannot provide overdraft facilities or hold client funds as deposits. For high-volume cross-border transactions, a tier-1 bank is more robust.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity. The legal representative (gérant) and any beneficial owners (UBOs) with >25% ownership must appear in person at a branch or with a notarized power of attorney. Remote opening is possible for certain banks if the company has an existing relationship or if using a digital onboarding platform, but the ACPR requires enhanced due diligence for non-resident directors. For a French SARL with non-resident shareholders, the bank will likely require a physical meeting with the gérant (manager) at the bank's premises or a French consulate/notary to verify identity. Some banks (e.g., BNP Paribas) offer remote video KYC for EU residents, but for non-EU directors, physical presence is mandatory. The mandate is to ensure compliance with the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier) and the 4th EU AML Directive.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., tax haven or sanctioned country)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide source of wealth documentation (bank statements, tax returns, audited financials), proof of legitimate business activity, and a clear organizational chart. Obtain a legal opinion from a French attorney confirming the legitimacy of the ownership structure. Ensure all UBOs are identified and their identity verified with passport copies and proof of address. If the jurisdiction is on FATF grey list, provide enhanced due diligence reports and a business rationale for the ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., rapid in-and-out transfers, high volume of small payments from consumers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed business model description, subscription contracts, and evidence of the EdTech platform's operations. Maintain a transaction monitoring system and be prepared to explain the expected payment flows. Provide audited financial statements and a cash flow forecast. The bank may require a compliance officer to sign off on the account's purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient corporate substance (e.g., no physical office, no employees in France)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a lease agreement for a registered office, employment contracts for local staff, and evidence of local management. If the SARL is a holding or shell, the bank may reject the application. Demonstrate that the company has real economic activity in France, such as a local marketing team or customer support. Provide a business plan and tax registration (SIRET number).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency or high-risk payment processor involvement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: If the company uses crypto for treasury, provide a clear policy and ensure all conversions are through regulated exchanges. For payment processors, ensure they are licensed and provide a contract. The bank may require a compliance opinion from a third-party AML expert.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For capital injection from shareholders (e.g., from a parent company or investors), the funds must be transferred via SWIFT MT103 with a clear purpose code. For equity contributions, use the purpose code 'S0101' (Direct investment - equity capital) or 'S0102' (Direct investment - other capital) as per the Banque de France's balance-of-payments classification. The transfer must be accompanied by a copy of the shareholders' resolution and the capital increase deed. For loans, use purpose code 'S0201' (Loans and credits) and ensure the loan agreement is documented. The bank will require a declaration to the Banque de France if the amount exceeds €15,000. The funds must be credited to a French bank account in EUR; if the injection is in foreign currency, the bank will convert it at the prevailing rate, and the company must report the transaction. For capital escrow, the funds are held in a blocked account until the SARL is fully registered, then released to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (e.g., paying for software licenses, marketing services, or content licensing), the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers. For larger transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) may be used, but for an EdTech company, MT103 is standard. The bank will require supporting documents (invoices, contracts) to comply with French foreign exchange regulations. For recurring payments to EU suppliers, SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) transfers are efficient and low-cost. For non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is used. The company must ensure that the purpose code on the transfer matches the nature of the payment (e.g., 'S0301' for services, 'S0401' for royalties). For disbursements to Apple and Google (for IAP and Play Billing), the company will receive funds from these platforms, not disburse to them; the outbound flows are for operational expenses. The bank may require a list of expected counterparties and their jurisdictions to pre-clear the account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (FX Forwards) with a maturity up to 12 months, available from French banks for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major currencies. These are OTC derivatives and require an ISDA or French master agreement.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are permissible for currencies with convertibility restrictions, but for the EdTech's main currencies (USD, GBP, CNY), NDFs are not necessary as they are fully convertible. However, if the company has exposure to emerging market currencies (e.g., INR, BRL), NDFs can be used.
Currency swaps (FX Swaps) for managing short-term liquidity and rolling over positions. These are allowed under French law and are subject to EMIR reporting requirements.
Options (FX options) are also permissible, but they are less common for small companies due to premium costs. The bank will require a credit line or collateral for any derivative transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax result declaration (liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD and attachments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; for an off-cycle fiscal year, within six months of the year-end date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after formal notice triggers a progressive late-filing surcharge of up to 40% of the assessed tax, monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% for each month, and compulsory assessment by DGFIP; persistent non-filing may expose directors to collection actions and disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of statutory accounts and allocation of result by the shareholders (assemblée générale ordinaire annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record maintained at the registered office; minutes form the supporting document for the RCS accounts deposit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed within six months after the financial year-end, unless extended by court order; calendar-year SARL commonly approves before 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the shareholders' meeting can be ordered by court on petition of any shareholder; persistent default exposes the company to administrative strike-off from the RCS and personal liability for resulting damage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements (bilan, compte de résultat, annexe), management report, and statutory auditor's report when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (commercial registry / Registre National des Entreprises, submitted via the electronic formalities system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholders' approval and no later than seven months after the financial year-end; a calendar-year SARL must normally file by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The court may issue an injunction with a coercive fine (astreinte) against the managers; failure to comply after formal notice may lead to administrative strike-off, loss of Kbis validity, and, where relevant, prohibition of the continuation of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration verification and update filing when ownership changes (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Registre National des Entreprises (INPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual standalone deadline; each qualifying change in beneficial ownership must be re-filed within 30 days. Internal register audit should be performed annually before the AG approval of accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate filing of a required update is sanctionable by criminal fine up to EUR 7,500 for the entity and possible director criminal liability; the company's standing and RCS extracts may be blocked during non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local economic contribution return (cotisation foncière des entreprises / CFE data declaration for CET)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual tax liasse; for a calendar-year SARL, due by the second business day after 1 May, or within six months after the close for an off-cycle year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare correctly leads to automatic application of the minimum taxable base, statutory late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, and a late-filing surcharge; unpaid CFE can be recovered by tax enforcement measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory when the SARL exceeds, at closing date, at least two of three thresholds: total balance-sheet assets above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover after tax above EUR 8,000,000; average full-time workforce above 50 employees during the financial year. Mandatory auditor appointment may also be triggered by corporate group status, public offering of securities, or court-appointed partnership/joint audit circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual accounts must be prepared under French GAAP, applying the Plan Comptable Général and ANC Regulation No. 2018-07 as amended, with applicable small- and micro-entity simplification exemptions; EU-IFRS may be adopted for consolidated financial statements only, not for the SARL's separate statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not mandate a separate annual UBO confirmation filing. The manager must file a new beneficial-owner declaration within 30 days of any change in shareholding, voting rights, or control. At Stage 5 the manager conducts an annual register audit comparing the statutory share register, transfer records, and control facts against the last UBO declaration lodged with the RCS, and files an update if any change occurred; if there is no change, no further annual government filing is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des mouvements de parts sociales / titres)
Register of Directors' decisions - Managers' decisions book (Registre des décisions de la gérance)
Minute book (Registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées générales et consultations écrites)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2022; qualifying small enterprises benefit from a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 profit for SMEs meeting the EUR 10 million turnover test and the capital-holding test (at least 75% held by individuals); research tax credit (CIR) up to 30% on eligible R&D expenditure; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% on qualifying innovation expenses for SMEs; Young Innovative Company (JEI) regime granting corporate income tax exemption up to EUR 100,000 profit per year and social contribution exemptions; reduced 12.8% rate for long-term capital gains on shareholdings under the mother-daughter participation regime.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_and_carryback_regi: Tax losses carry forward indefinitely, but annual utilization is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding that threshold. A carryback (report en arrière) is available limited to EUR 1,000,000 per fiscal year and may be credited against prior years' profits within a five-year horizon.
corporate_income_tax_regime.additional_levies: A 3.3% social surcharge (contribution sociale sur l'impôt sur les sociétés) applies where annual turnover exceeds EUR 7,630,000 and corporate income tax due exceeds EUR 763,000; CVAE value-added tax has been progressively abolished for production activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.applicable_to_edtech_subscription_model: Subscription revenues from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing constitute taxable turnover on a gross basis; commissions retained by app stores are deductible expenses in the SARL's audited accounts, but the reported net revenue must reconcile with platform statements for tax inspection purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats) with the 2050-SD to 2059-SD annexes; submitted electronically through the professional e-filing portal impots.gouv.fr (Espace professionnel, EDI-TDFC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return and annexes must be e-filed by the second business day after 1 May of the following year (typically 3-6 May). For off-calendar or shortened fiscal years, the deadline is within three months of fiscal year-end. Quarterly advance instalments (acomptes) are due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December; the balance (solde) is payable at the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office, SIRET number, NAF/APE code (6201Z for computer programming activities), and fiscal year opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French registered office even where the sole manager resides abroad. A non-resident manager does not exempt the SARL from filing; tax residence of each shareholder and manager must be disclosed accurately to support withholding tax and treaty analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after accounting result adjustments including depreciation recapture, disallowed expenses (e.g., non-deductible fines, 10% cap on certain luxury vehicles), exempt participation income, and capital gains or allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income of the SARL as a French tax resident. Apply the 15% reduced rate to the first EUR 42,500 of profit only where the SME criteria are certified; non-resident shareholders' advance payments to the SARL must be reclassified if disguised as equity or if no interest is charged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforwards utilized in the current year and the remaining loss balance available for future years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the annual utilization cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above that amount. Foreign branch losses and losses of foreign subsidiaries are not deductible against French profits unless expressly permitted under a tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full balance sheet including intangible assets (acquired or developed software), deferred revenue related to subscriptions, receivables from app stores, shareholder current accounts, and intra-group borrowings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose shareholder current accounts (comptes courants d'associés). Excessive or interest-free loans from non-resident shareholders attract transfer pricing adjustments, deemed interest rules, and hidden distribution scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD – Tax payable summary (Impôt sur les sociétés)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the 15% reduced tax and 25% standard tax, deduction of advance payments, and the final balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No treaty credit is applied at this stage for foreign taxes, and no exemption for dividends is granted without the formal parent-subsidiary regime claim; the SARL must certify the deduction of the app store platform fees with supporting statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of subsidiaries and participating interests exceeding 10% held during the fiscal year, with book value, percentage held, and results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all foreign participations. A French SARL holding interests in low-tax foreign entities is subject to CFC attribution rules under article 209 B of the CGI for passive income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: 10% late-filing increase (majoration) on the unpaid tax; 40% penalty if no return is filed within 30 days after a formal demerit notice (mise en demeure); 80% penalty for concealed or hidden activity. Late payment: 5% penalty plus monthly late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) at 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum). A further fixed fine of EUR 150 applies for materially incomplete financial statements, and persistent default can trigger loss of good standing and registry sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividend withholding under article 119 bis 2 of the French General Tax Code (CGI): 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders; 12.8% for non-resident individual shareholders, with applicable social levies in the absence of treaty protection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the distributing SARL must obtain, before payment, a sworn statement (affidavit) from the recipient confirming: non-French tax residence, genuine establishment in the treaty or EU state, a direct shareholding equal to or exceeding 10% (or the lower treaty threshold), a two-year minimum holding commitment where required, and sole beneficial ownership of the income. A valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign revenue authority must be attached, and the complete file submitted to the competent French fiscal service (SIE). The relief is granted provisionally at source and may be reversed on audit if substance and beneficial ownership are absent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and licence fees paid to non-residents for industrial, commercial, or intellectual property exploited in France are subject to statutory withholding of 33-1/3% under article 182 B of the CGI, generally reduced to 0% or 5% under France's double tax treaties. Interest paid to non-resident lenders on arm's length loans is generally exempt from French withholding tax, with most DTAs providing a 0% rate; payments to non-cooperative states or disguised profit distributions remain exposed to withholding reassessment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File, 'fichier des prix de transfert') applies to enterprises established in France with annual turnover above EUR 50,000,000 or more than 200 employees, including foreign-owned French subsidiaries and groups satisfying those thresholds. Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply Economic Substance Regulations of the offshore model. However, a French SARL must demonstrate genuine substance through its registered office, operational management exercised in France, payroll, premises, decision-making functions, and risk-taking capacity. Substance is enforced through the abuse-of-law doctrine (article L.64 of the LPF), the general anti-abuse rule, CFC rules, anti-hybrid provisions, the OECD BEPS minimum standards, and the Pillar Two global minimum tax of 15% for large groups. A shell SARL whose IP and digital platform functions are managed abroad without French substance will be treated as managed and controlled outside France or disregarded for treaty and directive benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of Apple IAP / Google Play Billing subscription revenues, fictitious deductions for platform commissions, backdated contracts, or failure to declare the commercial activity of the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under article 1741 CGI: criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, increased to EUR 750,000 and 7 years for aggravated cases (organized gang, use of offshore vehicles, or international concealment). Tax reassessment carries an 80% penalty for hidden activity plus 0.20% monthly interest and confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is criminally liable as perpetrator or accomplice. Courts may impose a management ban, travel ban, driving licence suspension, or committal orders for unpaid fines and taxes. The corporate veil is pierced where the manager's gross fault (faute lourde) caused the company's default or where the company is a mere facade for personal enrichment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting an IP holding shell in a zero-tax jurisdiction without employees, premises, or functions to strip the SARL's EdTech profits out of France, or artificially routing subscription royalties through a foreign group entity while management and development remain in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of article L.64 of the LPF disregards the abusive transaction and reallocates profits to the French entity; an 80% penalty applies for abuse of law, plus 0.20% monthly interest. The GAAR is complemented by the CFC rules of article 209 B CGI for low-tax passive income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager who initiated the artificial scheme in his own interest is personally liable for the reassessed tax debt. Criminal prosecution under article 1741 may follow, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000; asset attachments and exit bans are available coercive measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / False Treaty or Directive Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident shareholder claiming zero-rate dividend withholding through a paper EU holding company without premises, employees, business risk, or commercial purpose (letter-box company).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive or double tax treaty benefit, recharacterization of the dividend at the statutory 25% withholding rate, plus interest and penalties. The distributing SARL may be held jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax if it failed to obtain, prior to payment, a valid sworn statement and tax residence certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The French gérant who certified false substance statements is liable for restitution of the unpaid withholding tax. In aggravated patterns, criminal liability for fraud, forgery or issuance of false attestations may apply, with sentences up to 5 years' imprisonment and fines up to EUR 375,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, update, or produce the Master File and Local File upon the tax administration's formal request under article L.13 AA of the LPF, or pricing of intra-group IP royalties, app store commissions, or management fees inconsistent with the arm's length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of EUR 15,000 per fiscal year for failure to present the transfer pricing documentation; reassessment of shifted profits with a 40% penalty for bad faith or 80% for fraudulent concealment, plus 0.20% monthly interest. Late or missing Country-by-Country notification carries an additional EUR 15,000 fine per entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the transfer price was fixed personally by the gérant with gross negligence, the manager can be held jointly liable for the deficiency. Veil-piercing occurs in exceptional circumstances, exposing the manager's personal estate to collection and confiscation measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering in Digital Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funnelling Apple IAP / Google Play subscription revenue through personal accounts, structured small-volume transfers to avoid scrutiny, or using opaque payment intermediaries to launder fraud proceeds or conceal taxable turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the French Monetary and Financial Code anti-money-laundering obligations can trigger fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for repeat offences. Tax fraud sanctions under article 1741 CGI are cumulative, and the proceeds of the offence are subject to confiscation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A natural-person gérant convicted of money laundering (blanchiment) faces up to 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, plus professional bans and travel bans. Civil liability actions by creditors or the tax administration may reach the manager's personal assets.
